context:
Start from the already-correct canonical surface in
`benchbox/cli/platform_defaults.py` and the current ClickHouse platform option
registration, then push that contract outward to older compatibility layers.
Add one normalizer in the ClickHouse package, reuse it at the adapter and
metadata boundary, and migrate helper outputs to canonical `deployment_mode`
writes.

Treat docs and tests as part of the contract, not cleanup afterthoughts. The
CLI currently uses global `--mode` for execution mode, so ClickHouse docs must
stop teaching deployment selection through that flag. Update tests to lock in

description:
ClickHouse deployment selection still has split vocabulary and behavior across
the repo. The canonical path is already `deployment_mode` with `local` and
`server` in `benchbox/cli/platform_defaults.py`, ClickHouse platform option
registration, and adapter-factory wiring. But several older surfaces still
emit or teach a different contract:

- `benchbox/cli/config.py` still exposes `--mode` with `server|embedded`
- `benchbox/core/config_utils.py` still writes `mode` instead of `deployment_mode`
- `benchbox/platforms/clickhouse/adapter.py` and `metadata.py` only read
  `deployment_mode`, so old callers sending `mode="server"` can silently
  fall back to local behavior
- `benchbox/platforms/clickhouse/diagnostics.py` emits `metadata["mode"]`
- docs and examples still teach `--mode=local`, "embedded mode", or
  `clickhouse:cloud`

This drift is no longer cosmetic. The global `benchbox run --mode` flag now
means SQL-vs-DataFrame execution mode, so docs telling users to pass
`--mode=local` for ClickHouse deployment are actively wrong. Meanwhile legacy
helper paths can still build config using `mode`, which the adapter boundary
may ignore. The result is an ambiguous and partially broken contract for
local/server selection.

This TODO standardizes on `deployment_mode` as the only canonical ClickHouse
selector, keeps `mode` and `embedded` as compatibility-only inputs during a
transition window, and removes stale docs/examples that still present
ClickHouse Cloud as a deployment mode of the base `clickhouse` platform.

This item is complete only as compatibility groundwork. Its remaining
docs/help/test cleanup is intentionally absorbed by
`first-class-clickhouse-local-server-cloud-platforms`, which replaces the
long-term public contract with first-class `clickhouse-local`,
`clickhouse-server`, and `clickhouse-cloud` platform names.
